ht-base-1.command: python bench/run.py --name ht-base-1 --gpu 0 --model unsloth/Qwen3-8B-GGUF@a6adef130ffb/Qwen3-8B-Q4_K_M.gguf --lock plans/unsloth/Qwen3-8B-GGUF/Qwen3-8B-Q4_K_M@120307ba529eb243/rtx-3090/cu130-torch2.11/4.lock --backends holon --traces bench/traces/decode_b64.jsonl bench/traces/agent.jsonl --rounds 1 --blocking-sync --evidence-dir local/tmp/k-build/k4/ht
ht-base-1.method: In-process engines driven by bench/driver.py, one scheduling step per call; client-side timestamps taken when a step returns a token. TTFT = first token - release (arrival, or previous turn's last token + gap); TPOT = (last - first) / (tokens - 1) per request; throughput = output tokens / (last token - first release). Decode steps = steps at peak batch that return no first token; decode tok/s = their tokens / their wall time. Max gap = a request's largest time between two deliveries after its first token. Repeated share = output tokens ending a 16-gram already in their request's prompt or output / output tokens. Paired TTFT = the median over (round, session, turn) of TTFT / the first backend's TTFT in the same round. CPU ms/step = time.process_time() delta around step() on those steps, measured with --blocking-sync (CUDA primary context in blocking-sync mode and torch events created blocking, so waiting for the GPU sleeps and is not counted). Greedy, ignore_eos, fixed output lengths; warmup on the same shapes with other prompt tokens, excluded. HTTP backends (llamaserver, holon_http; bench/backends/http.py): streamed requests, a token timestamped when its chunk arrives; their 'steps' are client polls, so decode tok/s and CPU ms/step do not apply to them.
